observations: body L1-L2: in the head the dash after «b)» measures 10.3 pt; the dash after «Coptorum.» 10.4 pt.
body L4, L6, L10, L13-L14, L25, L28, L30-L31: the dashes of «al–Battānī», «’l–qarnayn», «1825–26», «30–32», «Graecos–Aegyptios» and «Graeci–Aegyptii» are long dashes (5.2 to 5.8 pt).
body L2: the first e of «tres» prints broken, like c.

body L5-L7: 29 August 25 B.C. (proleptic Julian calendar) was a Friday. From 1 September 312 B.C., the epoch of the era of Dhū ’l-qarnayn in al-Battānī, to 29 August 25 B.C. are 104824 days, 287 Julian years (104827 days) less 3 days.
body L11: 1 thōth 719 of Nabonassar, 718 × 365 days after 26 February 747 B.C., is 31 August 30 B.C., a Sunday.
body L12: «annos» is printed twice; kept as printed.
body L16: 1460 Julian years of 365 1/4 days and 1461 vague years of 365 days are both 533265 days.

body L21-L24: in the proleptic Julian calendar 30 August 26 B.C. was a Thursday, not a Friday as printed; 29 August 25 B.C. (L24) was a Friday. The two dates are 365 days apart, since 25 B.C. is a leap year, so they cannot both fall on a Friday; kept as printed. 30 August 26 B.C. is the 1 thōth of the year before a Julian leap year, 29 August 25 B.C. that of a common year.
body L30: a speck before «Addit» is not transcribed.

notes_left L5-L6: the dashes of «’l–āthār» and «261–262» measure 4.2 and 4.3 pt, longer than the hyphens of the notes (3.1 to 3.4 pt), and are transcribed as long dashes; «p 261–262» has no period after the p, as printed.
notes_left L6, L8: «al-Maṣ‘ūdī» in L6 has a dot under the s, «al-Mas‘ūdī» in L8 none; kept as printed. In L6 the first s of «Nabonassaris» prints broken, as a small mark.
notes_left L8, L10: the dash after «198.» measures 8.6 pt; the sign of equality in L10 7.8 pt, and the closing parenthesis after «23» prints only as a faint mark.
notes_right L1: the dash after «fuisse.» measures 7.0 pt; note 2 goes on here from the left column.
notes_right L8-L10: the hyphens of «239-244» and «293-294» measure 3.0 and 3.5 pt; «Inscri-» is divided with a raised dot; the e of «1ᵉ» is raised in both places.
